title: Crotchets and minims
summary: Find the steady pulse, then meet the 1-beat crotchet and the 2-beat minim.

hook.text: First-aiders learn to press on the chest in time with *Stayin' Alive*. Why that song? Because something in it ticks along as evenly as a clock. Press play, then tap your foot to this tune. Can you feel the tick?

explore.text: Your turn. A click will tick away. Start by tapping the pad once on every click. Then get sneaky: tap, let one click go by, and tap again. Same click, but each tap now lasts twice as long.
explore.goal: Tap along with all 8 short notes, then all 4 long ones.

cards.text: That steady tick you tapped is the [[pulse|pulse]]. Each tick is one [[beat|beat]]. The pulse carries on even when a tune holds a long note, like a clock ticking away under the music.

A note that lasts 1 beat is a [[crotchet|crotchet]]: a filled-in head with a stem. A note that lasts 2 beats is a [[minim|minim]]: same stem, but a hollow head. Easy way to remember: hollow means hold.

Music is packed into boxes called [[bar|bars]], split up by upright [[bar-line|bar lines]]. Every [[bar|bar]] in this lesson holds 4 beats: 4 [[crotchet|crotchets]], 2 [[minim|minims]], or a mix. (The two 4s at the start say so. More on them next lesson.)

alternative.text: Think of walking. Each footstep is one beat. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] is one step: say "walk". A [[minim|minim]] takes two steps of time: say "sta-ay" and hold it. Now say this in time with your feet: walk, walk, sta-ay. You just read the [[bar|bar]] below.

questions.prompt: Tap the [[pulse|pulse]]: one tap on every click, 8 taps in all. Every note here is a [[crotchet|crotchet]], so each one gets 1 beat.
questions.hint: Do not chase the click. Listen to the count-in, feel how far apart the clicks are, then tap with them like footsteps.

questions.prompt: Listen to clip A and clip B. Which one is made of [[minim|minims]]?
questions.hint: Tap a steady beat while you listen. Each [[minim|minim]] lasts for 2 of your taps.

options.reason: Clip A is all short notes of 1 beat each, so those are [[crotchet|crotchets]]. The [[minim|minims]] are the slow 2-beat notes in clip B.

questions.prompt: This [[bar|bar]] needs 4 beats but only has 2. Add **one** note to fill it.
questions.hint: Two [[crotchet|crotchets]] make 2 beats. Which single note is worth the 2 beats still missing?

questions.prompt: Listen, then tap this rhythm. One tap for each note. Remember: hollow means hold.
questions.hint: Say it as you tap: "walk" for each [[crotchet|crotchet]], "sta-ay" for each [[minim|minim]]. Each [[minim|minim]] gets one tap, then you wait for its second beat.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. One tap for each note.
questions.hint: A [[minim|minim]] gets one tap, then you wait for its second beat before the next note.

questions.prompt: Tap this rhythm. Watch out: it starts with a long note.
questions.hint: The first note is a [[minim|minim]]. Tap it on the first click, then let the second click go by.
Hollow means hold. The [[crotchet|crotchet]] is the short one, so its head is not hollow.

options.reason: That head is hollow, so it is a [[minim|minim]] and lasts 2 beats. The [[crotchet|crotchet]] has a filled-in head.
That note has no stem, and it is hollow. A [[crotchet|crotchet]] has a filled-in head and a stem.

questions.prompt: How many beats does a [[minim|minim]] last?
questions.hint: Think "walk, walk, sta-ay". How many footsteps does "sta-ay" take?

options.reason: The 1-beat note is the [[crotchet|crotchet]]. A [[minim|minim]] is the hollow one, and hollow means hold: it lasts 2 beats.
4 beats would fill a whole [[bar|bar]] in this lesson. A [[minim|minim]] fills half of one: 2 beats.

questions.prompt: Add **one** note to fill this [[bar|bar]] with 4 beats.
questions.hint: Add up what is there: a [[minim|minim]] is 2 beats and a [[crotchet|crotchet]] is 1. How many are missing?
Listen for the long note. Does it come first or last?

options.reason: That [[bar|bar]] starts with its long note. The one you heard went short, short, long.
That [[bar|bar]] has only two notes, both long. You heard three notes: short, short, long.

questions.prompt: Every [[bar|bar]] here should hold 4 beats. One [[bar|bar]] has too many. Tap it.
questions.hint: Count each [[bar|bar]]: 1 for every filled-in note, 2 for every hollow one.

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 2 has 5 beats: a [[minim|minim]] (2), a [[crotchet|crotchet]] (1) and another [[minim|minim]] (2). That is one beat too many.

questions.prompt: A tune lands on a long note and holds it. What does the [[pulse|pulse]] do?
questions.hint: Think back to your long taps on the pad. What was the click doing while you waited?

face.text: It keeps ticking at the same speed
It stops until the next note

options.reason: The [[pulse|pulse]] never waits for the tune. It kept ticking under your long taps, and it does the same under any long note.
Long notes do not slow the [[pulse|pulse]]. The beats stay the same distance apart; the note just lasts for more of them.

points: The [[pulse|pulse]] is the steady tick under the music. Each tick is one [[beat|beat]].
A [[crotchet|crotchet]] has a filled-in head and a stem. It lasts 1 beat.
A [[minim|minim]] has a hollow head and a stem. It lasts 2 beats: hollow means hold.
[[bar-line|Bar lines]] split music into [[bar|bars]]. In this lesson every [[bar|bar]] holds 4 beats.
